insider_note: Coding against non-coding, and present against absent in the mature RNA. Two contrasts each.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Exons
steps.margin_note: Coding, present in mature RNA, and the name. Four lines.
lines: EXONS are the CODING sequences of a gene.
They APPEAR in the mature, processed RNA.
They are EXPRESSED — which is what the name
steps.why: Only the exons reach the ribosome, so only they decide the amino acid sequence of the protein.
common_mistakes: Saying exons are removed. INTRONS are removed; exons are kept.
Saying exons do not code. Exons are the CODING parts.

steps.label: Introns
steps.margin_note: Mirror the exon lines, then name splicing.

lines.text: Exons stay in the message; introns are cut out

lines: They do NOT appear in the mature, processed RNA.
They are cut out during SPLICING, and the exons
steps.why: Splicing removes the introns and joins the exons, which is why the mature message is shorter than the gene it came from.
common_mistakes: Saying introns are translated. They are removed BEFORE translation.
Not naming splicing. It is the process that removes them.
steps.memory_tip: INtrons are INtervening, and they come out.
